newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK RALLY PUSHES HUNGARY BUX TO RECORD.
newsitem.headline: TVK RALLY PUSHES HUNGARY BUX TO RECORD.

text.p: Hungarian stocks traded firmer on Wednesday pushing the BUX index to record territory as they were benefiting from demand after the expiry of June futures on Tuesday and from a positive market sentiment induced by a surge in chemicals TVK shares, traders said.
At 1100 GMT the BUX index stood at 6,448.09 points, up 134.91.
Two of Wednesday's losers, pharmaceuticals Egis Rt and OTP Bank gained more than three percent, after Tuesday's expiry of June BUX futures forced many investors to unload many stocks at any price.
"Their rise was obviously due to the fact that they had no sellers after Tuesday's unload," one trader said.
At 1047 GMT Egis traded at 11,900 forints, up 400 and at 1051 GMT OTP traded at 4,600 forints, up 150.
Also, a record run in TVK shares spread positive market sentiment over other stocks, including oil company MOL which rallied to a new record high of 3,800 forints before giving up a little.
At 1047 GMT MOL traded at 3,795 forints, up 65.

TVK was surging to new record levels of 3,255 forints and $17.75 in early trading in Budapest and London, respectively, still benefiting from market talks of an imminent payout by the state to the company, traders said.
TVK is expected to cash in five billion forints and an additional one billion of accumulated interest under the provisions of Hungary's previous privatisation law.
